\section{Hypercontractivity --- Products --- Tensorization}
%%% generated by the blueprint pipeline from TCSlib.BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.Products.Tensorization
\subsection*{Hypercontractivity --- Products --- Tensorization: Introduction}
Nonnegative finite coordinate kernels tensorize both pairing bounds and moment-norm contractions. The weights and kernels are explicit and need not be normalized.

\subsection*{Hypercontractivity --- Products --- Tensorization: Results}

\begin{theorem}[Tensorization of pairing estimates]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteTensorization.pair_tensorization}
\leanok
\difficulty{6}
Let $n$ be a natural number, let each $\Omega_i$ be finite, and let
$w_i:\Omega_i\to\mathbb R$ and $k_i:\Omega_i\times\Omega_i\to\mathbb R$ be nonnegative.
Let $p,r\in\mathbb R$ satisfy $1\le p$ and $1\le r$. Suppose that for every coordinate
$i$ and every pair of real-valued functions $u,v$ on $\Omega_i$,
$\sum_{x,y}k_i(x,y)u(x)v(y)\le\left(\sum_xw_i(x)|u(x)|^p\right)^{1/p}\left(\sum_yw_i(y)|v(y)|^r\right)^{1/r}$.
Then for all real-valued $f,g$ on $\prod_i\Omega_i$, $\sum_{x,y}\left(\prod_i
k_i(x_i,y_i)\right)f(x)g(y)\le\left(\sum_x\left(\prod_iw_i(x_i)\right)|f(x)|^p\right)^{1/p}\left(\sum_y\left(\prod_iw_i(y_i)\right)|g(y)|^r\right)^{1/r}$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Tensorization of norm contractions]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteTensorization.norm_tensorization}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteNorms.norm_le_of_pairing, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteNorms.weighted_holder, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteTensorization.pair_tensorization}
\difficulty{5}
Let $n$ be a natural number, let each $\Omega_i$ be finite, and let
$w_i:\Omega_i\to\mathbb R$ and $k_i:\Omega_i\times\Omega_i\to\mathbb R$ be nonnegative.
Let $p,q\in\mathbb R$ satisfy $1\le p$ and $1<q$. Suppose that for every coordinate $i$
and every $h:\Omega_i\to\mathbb R$, $\left(\sum_y w_i(y)\left|\sum_x
k_i(y,x)h(x)\right|^q\right)^{1/q}\le\left(\sum_xw_i(x)|h(x)|^p\right)^{1/p}$. Then for
every real-valued $f$ on $\prod_i\Omega_i$,
$\left(\sum_y\left(\prod_iw_i(y_i)\right)\left|\sum_x\left(\prod_i
k_i(y_i,x_i)\right)f(x)\right|^q\right)^{1/q}\le\left(\sum_x\left(\prod_iw_i(x_i)\right)|f(x)|^p\right)^{1/p}$.
\end{theorem}
